sections.title: Fill in the blanks and write the correct answers.

questions.q: To prepare pastry dough, we need ________ water for mixing.
Eclair is made from ________ paste.
Profiteroles are made from ________ paste.
The main ingredients to prepare puff pastry are fat and ________.
The word ________ is same as paste.
Flour with good quality gluten is required for ________ pastry.
________ juice is added to strengthen the gluten in flaky and puff pastry.
A long thin shell of the same paste as cream puffs is called ________.
Puff pastry contains fat and flour in the ratio of ________.
In choux paste, the eggs are added only after the mixture has ________.

sections.title: State whether the following statements are True or False.

questions.q: Cheese straws are made from short crust paste.
questions.answer: False. They are made from puff (or flaky) pastry.

questions.q: Lemon juice may be added while making puff pastry.
Puff pastry requires strong flour.
All the fat in puff paste is folded in one rolling.
When dough is over rolled, the product becomes hard.
Puff and flaky pastes always give different products.
questions.answer: False. The products that can be made are the same with a slight variation in texture.

questions.q: The amount of fat used in flaky paste is more than that in puff paste.
questions.answer: False. Puff paste has more fat (1:1) than flaky paste (3/4:1).

questions.q: Warm or tap water should be used for mixing pastry.
Eclairs shrink in size if they are removed too quickly from the oven.
questions.answer: True. The oven door is opened for another 10 minutes of baking to prevent shrinking.

sections.title: Answer the following questions (five points each).

questions.q: Give any five suggestions for preparing a good paste.
questions.answer: (i) Work in a cool place and keep your hands cool. (ii) Sift the flour and salt to incorporate air. (iii) Use cold water and do not use too much. (iv) Handle the pastry as little and as lightly as possible. (v) Chill the pastry for 15-30 minutes after making and bake it in a fairly hot oven.

questions.q: Mention the steps of making choux paste.
questions.answer: (i) Put butter and water in a thick bottomed degchi and bring to boil. (ii) Add sieved flour all at one time, mixing vigorously. (iii) Cook on slow fire until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan. (iv) Cool to room temperature and add eggs one by one, mixing nicely. (v) Beat until firm enough to pipe and use as required.

questions.q: Name the basic 5 pastes made in bakery.
questions.answer: (i) Short crust paste. (ii) Flaky paste. (iii) Puff paste. (iv) Choux paste. (v) Danish paste.

questions.q: Differentiate between flaky pastry and puff pastry.
questions.answer: (i) Puff pastry has fat and flour in the ratio 1:1; flaky pastry has 3/4 fat to every kilogram of flour. (ii) In puff pastry all the fat is folded in at one rolling; in flaky pastry it is divided into three parts and folded in three rollings. (iii) Puff pastry has more layers; flaky pastry has fewer. (iv) Puff pastry has four empty rollings; flaky pastry has only one empty rolling.

questions.q: Why do we chill puff or flaky paste between different rollings? State the common faults of these pastries.
questions.answer: (i) Chilling keeps the fat firm so that it does not melt or break through the dough layers. (ii) It relaxes the gluten and makes rolling easier. (iii) Faults: too few layers due to insufficient resting and chilling or warm fat. (iv) Fat running out during baking due to a low baking temperature. (v) Hard and tough pastry due to too much water, over-kneading or a cool oven.
